355.title: Dispel level-three-or-lower spells on one explicit creature
355.body:
<!-- edda-271:dispel-low -->

Parent: #193 · Decision: #271 · Roadmap: #47. One reviewable PR; L; afk. Implementation fixture; not full spell/family support.

Source: [pinned SRD 5.2.1](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/srd/5.2/SRD_CC_v5.2.1.pdf), PDF pages 105, 106, 124, 179. SHA-256 `8974902d109d6e63672d7c490bde9ccf052410503d9cfa768237154fbc5e3d87`. Pin, attribution and adaptation: `docs/srd-5.2.1-conformance.md`.

## Exact fixture

An isolated authorized level-five Cleric fixture uses level-three Dispel Magic on a known creature carrying Shield of Faith and Bless from independent casters.

## Targets

One known creature within 120 feet and clear path; end every qualifying ongoing spell on that target. A multi-recipient cast loses only the targeted recipient link, not other recipients.

## Costs

Magic action, one level-three slot, V/S. Automatic ending for ongoing spells level three or lower; no ability check for these spells.

## Timing and mechanic boundary

Commit action cost, exact affected spell/link IDs and history together. Distinguish ending the target’s spell effect from ending its caster’s unrelated concentration.

Proposed mechanic keys (planning identifiers, not registered support): `spell.dispel.creature.low-level`, `effect.remove.recipient-link`. Reconcile with #194/#277/#278; keep unknown keys unavailable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Test several qualifying spells, suppressed same-name effects, unrelated targets/casters, no eligible spells (legal cast still costs), reload and exact removal once.
- [ ] Reject unknown spell levels, level-four-or-higher effects and object/magical-effect targets with an explicit unsupported reason until the bounded follow-up decides them. Isolated authorized fixture only; production eligibility requires exact #323 advancement child, not decision closure.
- [ ] Durable mutation fixtures: lock/revalidate all involved actors and effect revisions; save costs, dice, effect/link state, clock/turn and history in one transaction. Inject history-write failure and prove complete rollback; retry same action ID returns the committed receipt with no extra roll, charge or effect. Reload/reconnect resumes exact identities and pending timing.
- [ ] Disclosure negatives: preview never rolls/writes; reject foreign campaign/actor IDs, hidden recipients and forged costs/timing; public receipts omit private NPC HP, unobserved spells and tactics. Unknown facts fail closed with an explicit reason. Preserve unrelated JSON and legacy reads.
- [ ] For higher-level isolated fixtures, demonstrate authoritative test entitlement explicitly; do not treat imported spell data or closing a class investigation as player eligibility. Publish any missing production-eligibility implementation prerequisite before enabling discovery.

## Hard prerequisites

- #203
- #352

Only these are hard prerequisites: source record/contract owners and the exact shared fixture named above. Class production eligibility stays unavailable where explicitly excluded. Every terminal implementation directly blocks both #279 and #280. A spike must add all of its resulting terminal implementation blockers to both gates before closure; decision closure supplies no playable evidence.

## Verification

`go test -short -race ./...` and `go vet ./...`. Runtime PRs must additionally run isolated PostgreSQL handler tests with `-tags=integration`, injectable dice, rollback, receipt replay and reload (short tests do not include them). Changed UI requires build/lint and desktop/phone confirmation/reconnect journeys. Spike PRs validate source/manifest and read back every published body, parent and dependency, checking acyclicity.

## Boundaries and exclusions

Start in `internal/rules/srd521`, `internal/game`, `internal/engine`, `internal/combat` and relevant handler fixtures. Keep the shared web/TUI action path; no production migration execution or deployment. No general antimagic, curses, nonspell magic-item removal, object/area targeting, higher-level checks/upcasting or automatic class advancement. No Full Rules claim. Retain CC-BY-4.0 attribution and mark adaptations. Close from the merged PR.

356.title: Persist one Counterspell reaction window around Cure Wounds casting
356.body:
<!-- edda-271:counterspell-window -->

Parent: #193 · Decision: #271 · Roadmap: #47. One reviewable PR; L; afk. Implementation fixture; not full spell/family support.

Source: [pinned SRD 5.2.1](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/srd/5.2/SRD_CC_v5.2.1.pdf), PDF pages 105, 120, 179. SHA-256 `8974902d109d6e63672d7c490bde9ccf052410503d9cfa768237154fbc5e3d87`. Pin, attribution and adaptation: `docs/srd-5.2.1-conformance.md`.

## Exact fixture

A prepared Cleric attempts the existing level-one Cure Wounds self cast while one explicitly known authorized NPC Counterspell caster has a reaction and level-three slot.

## Targets

One visible known casting creature within 60 feet, with V/S/M casting observable and clear path. Use an isolated trusted NPC fixture, not a general monster caster entitlement.

## Costs

Counterspell: one Reaction, one level-three slot, S. Target Constitution save against reactor’s spell DC. Failure wastes target’s casting action/Bonus Action/Reaction but does not expend its spell slot; success permits original cast once.

## Timing and mechanic boundary

Suspend before original spell resolves or spends its slot; persist casting attempt and trigger identity plus actor’s spent casting time. Explicit react/decline and stale confirmation. Concentration replacement starts when casting starts, even if interrupted.

Proposed mechanic keys (planning identifiers, not registered support): `casting.pending-attempt`, `reaction.counterspell.constitution`, `casting.countered.slot-not-spent`. Reconcile with #194/#277/#278; keep unknown keys unavailable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Test failed and successful saves, decline, unavailable reaction, no components, unseen/foreign/out-of-range trigger, stale pending attempt, crash/reconnect before and after decision and duplicate confirmation.
- [ ] Persist original attempt, reaction cost, save and resume/cancel outcome atomically. If the target fails its Constitution save, the interrupted spell never heals and never spends the target slot; if the target succeeds, the original spell resolves and heals once. Existing opportunity-reaction flow remains bounded and intact.
- [ ] Durable mutation fixtures: lock/revalidate all involved actors and effect revisions; save costs, dice, effect/link state, clock/turn and history in one transaction. Inject history-write failure and prove complete rollback; retry same action ID returns the committed receipt with no extra roll, charge or effect. - [ ] For higher-level isolated fixtures, demonstrate authoritative test entitlement explicitly; do not treat imported spell data or closing a class investigation as player eligibility. Publish any missing production-eligibility implementation prerequisite before enabling discovery.

- #201

Wall of Stone
Level 5 Evocation (Druid, Sorcerer, Wizard)
Casting Time: Action
Range: 120 feet
Components: V, S, M (a cube of granite)
Duration: Concentration, up to 10 minutes
A nonmagical wall of solid stone springs into exis-
tence at a point you choose within range. The wall
is 6 inches thick and is composed of ten 10-foot-by-
10-foot panels. Each panel must be contiguous with
another panel. Alternatively, you can create 10-foot-
by-20-foot panels that are only 3 inches thick.
If the wall cuts through a creature’s space when
it appears, the creature is pushed to one side of the
wall (you choose which side). If a creature would
be surrounded on all sides by the wall (or the wall
and another solid surface), that creature can make
a Dexterity saving throw. On a success, it can use its
Reaction to move up to its Speed so that it is no lon-
ger enclosed by the wall.
The wall can have any shape you desire, though it
can’t occupy the same space as a creature or object.
The wall doesn’t need to be vertical or rest on a firm
foundation. It must, however, merge with and be
solidly supported by existing stone. Thus, you can
use this spell to bridge a chasm or create a ramp.
If you create a span greater than 20 feet in length,
you must halve the size of each panel to create sup-
ports. You can crudely shape the wall to create bat-
tlements and the like.
The wall is an object made of stone that can be
damaged and thus breached. Each panel has AC 15
and 30 Hit Points per inch of thickness, and it has
Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage. Reducing
a panel to 0 Hit Points destroys it and might cause
connected panels to collapse at the GM’s discretion.
If you maintain your Concentration on this spell
for its full duration, the wall becomes permanent
and can’t be dispelled. Otherwise, the wall disap-
pears when the spell ends.

Casting Time: Action
Range: 60 feet
Components: V, S, M (a caterpillar cocoon)

ceed on a Wisdom saving throw or shape-shift into
a Beast form for the duration. That form can be any
Beast you choose that has a Challenge Rating equal
to or less than the target’s (or the target’s level if
it doesn’t have a Challenge Rating). The target’s
game statistics are replaced by the stat block of the
chosen Beast, but the target retains its alignment,
personality, creature type, Hit Points, and Hit Point
Dice. See the “Animals” section of “Monsters” for a
sample of Beast stat blocks.
The target gains a number of Temporary Hit
Points equal to the Hit Points of the Beast form.
These Temporary Hit Points vanish if any remain
when the spell ends. The spell ends early on the tar-
get if it has no Temporary Hit Points left.
The target is limited in the actions it can perform
by the anatomy of its new form, and it can’t speak or
cast spells.
The target’s gear melds into the new form. The
creature can’t use or otherwise benefit from any of
that equipment.

Wall of Stone
Level 5 Evocation (Druid, Sorcerer, Wizard)
Casting Time: Action
Range: 120 feet
Components: V, S, M (a cube of granite)
Duration: Concentration, up to 10 minutes
A nonmagical wall of solid stone springs into exis-
tence at a point you choose within range. The wall
is 6 inches thick and is composed of ten 10-foot-by-
10-foot panels. Each panel must be contiguous with
another panel. Alternatively, you can create 10-foot-
by-20-foot panels that are only 3 inches thick.
If the wall cuts through a creature’s space when
it appears, the creature is pushed to one side of the
wall (you choose which side). If a creature would
be surrounded on all sides by the wall (or the wall
and another solid surface), that creature can make
a Dexterity saving throw. On a success, it can use its
Reaction to move up to its Speed so that it is no lon-
ger enclosed by the wall.
The wall can have any shape you desire, though it
can’t occupy the same space as a creature or object.
The wall doesn’t need to be vertical or rest on a firm
foundation. It must, however, merge with and be
solidly supported by existing stone. Thus, you can
use this spell to bridge a chasm or create a ramp.
If you create a span greater than 20 feet in length,
you must halve the size of each panel to create sup-
ports. You can crudely shape the wall to create bat-
tlements and the like.
The wall is an object made of stone that can be
damaged and thus breached. Each panel has AC 15
and 30 Hit Points per inch of thickness, and it has
Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage. Reducing
a panel to 0 Hit Points destroys it and might cause
connected panels to collapse at the GM’s discretion.
If you maintain your Concentration on this spell
for its full duration, the wall becomes permanent
and can’t be dispelled. Otherwise, the wall disap-
pears when the spell ends.

get if it has no Temporary Hit Points left.

by the anatomy of its new form, and it can’t speak or
cast spells.
The target’s gear melds into the new form. The
creature can’t use or otherwise benefit from any of
that equipment.

Scope and deterministic positive/negative fixtures: PDF183 Heroic Inspiration; Champion grant PDF49, Human Resourceful remains #333. One shared durable PC-held boolean pool, maximum one; generic receipt/provenance with NO automatic gains. Immediately after rolling ANY owned known typed die, may expend held Heroic Inspiration to reroll that single die and MUST use new face even when worse. Not only d20, not entire dice pool, not a later arbitrary history reroll. Deterministic bounded positive/negative adapters are mandatory for current shared-engine ability-check/saving-throw d20, weapon attack d20 and individual weapon-damage d8, existing healing dice, Fighter advancement d10/fixed-choice rejection, and individually typed feat/resource dice when their exact effect owner is qualified. Each die role names its existing resolver and immediate phase; keep unsupported/unregistered adapters unavailable. Preserve original face, chosen die identity, replacement face, final dependent outcome and source provenance; one immediate window, explicit use/decline, no intervening roll/action, immutable original receipt plus final replacement reconciliation. Source gain producers remain separate: Champion751 can grant ONLY during combat at start of own turn without it; Human Resourceful is owned by333, never enabled here. If a NEW gain arrives while already held, it is lost unless explicitly given to a PC who lacks it; transfer this new gain only, no stockpiling or invented transfer of previously held inspiration, no recursive duplicate gain. Overflow transfer requires known owned/authorized PC context, never foreign/NPC/hidden actors or private roll disclosures. Stable action/roll/gain IDs bind pool cost, die replacement, dependent effects and history atomically; reload/concurrent use applies once, all injected failure paths roll back cost/dice/effect/history. Bardic Inspiration512 remains a different resource and is not reused. No species/class eligibility or spell work. All feature/admission consumers require qualified typed adapter; generic pool presence does not qualify every roll. Parent50; exact native prerequisites61/64/65. Shared qualification paths: this terminal->279 and280; this terminal->751->728->337 and directly->728->337. Positive: a known owned ability-check die with secret DC and undisclosed outcome opens the immediate Heroic Inspiration use/decline window; a worse reroll must be kept, while the DC and outcome remain undisclosed. Negative: that same unknown outcome cannot open Tactical Mind or Indomitable, and hidden/foreign dice, stale windows and unregistered adapters cannot open Heroic Inspiration.

For each exact predicate below: deterministic positive and independently violated negative fixtures, unsupported/forged origin/level/owner rejection, inert prepare/cancel with no dice/state/history changes, explicit confirmed choice, stale revision rejection, stable action-ID replay after lost response and durable reload, concurrent confirmation applies once, atomic cost/dice/history/database rollback including injected write failures, no private DC/hidden target/lore disclosure. Shared engine through web AND trusted TUI: disabled/unavailable explanations, confirmation/cancel/reconnect/retry and keyboard/phone journeys. Injectable dice unit tests plus isolated PostgreSQL handler/state integration tests; frontend build/changed-file lint/behavior fixtures and TUI command tests. GOMAXPROCS=2 go test -p 2 -short -race ./... and GOMAXPROCS=2 go vet -p 2 ./... . Feature tests use isolated entitlements; only separately qualified admission/transition may grant them. Unknown outcomes never imply success/failure. Outcome-dependent reactions such as Tactical Mind and Indomitable require a disclosed qualifying outcome. Heroic Inspiration remains available immediately after an owned known die even when the DC and outcome are undisclosed. No inference, deployment, grants, coverage or Full Rules promotion from planning. For passive/automatic source benefits, confirmation belongs to the triggering action or turn; never invent an optional activation or extra action cost.

Absolute start/expiry seconds, maximum 600 seconds. Replace only the casting caster’s previous concentration. Equal-potency overlapping +2 AC applies once, latest casting active; ending it reveals an older still-live effect without restarting its clock.

Dispel Magic.title: Dispel level-three-or-lower spells on one explicit creature
Dispel Magic.body:
<!-- edda-271:dispel-low -->

Parent: #193 · Decision: #271 · Roadmap: #47. One reviewable PR; L; afk. Implementation fixture; not full spell/family support.

Source: [pinned SRD 5.2.1](https://media.dndbeyond.com/compendium-images/srd/5.2/SRD_CC_v5.2.1.pdf), PDF pages 105, 106, 124, 179. SHA-256 `8974902d109d6e63672d7c490bde9ccf052410503d9cfa768237154fbc5e3d87`. Pin, attribution and adaptation: `docs/srd-5.2.1-conformance.md`.

## Exact fixture

An isolated authorized level-five Cleric fixture uses level-three Dispel Magic on a known creature carrying Shield of Faith and Bless from independent casters.

## Targets

One known creature within 120 feet and clear path; end every qualifying ongoing spell on that target. A multi-recipient cast loses only the targeted recipient link, not other recipients.

## Costs

Magic action, one level-three slot, V/S. Automatic ending for ongoing spells level three or lower; no ability check for these spells.

## Timing and mechanic boundary

Commit action cost, exact affected spell/link IDs and history together. Distinguish ending the target’s spell effect from ending its caster’s unrelated concentration.

Proposed mechanic keys (planning identifiers, not registered support): `spell.dispel.creature.low-level`, `effect.remove.recipient-link`. Reconcile with #194/#277/#278; keep unknown keys unavailable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Test several qualifying spells, suppressed same-name effects, unrelated targets/casters, no eligible spells (legal cast still costs), reload and exact removal once.
- [ ] Reject unknown spell levels, level-four-or-higher effects and object/magical-effect targets with an explicit unsupported reason until the bounded follow-up decides them. Isolated authorized fixture only; production eligibility requires exact #323 advancement child, not decision closure.
- [ ] Durable mutation fixtures: lock/revalidate all involved actors and effect revisions; save costs, dice, effect/link state, clock/turn and history in one transaction. Inject history-write failure and prove complete rollback; retry same action ID returns the committed receipt with no extra roll, charge or effect. Reload/reconnect resumes exact identities and pending timing.
- [ ] Disclosure negatives: preview never rolls/writes; reject foreign campaign/actor IDs, hidden recipients and forged costs/timing; public receipts omit private NPC HP, unobserved spells and tactics. Unknown facts fail closed with an explicit reason. Preserve unrelated JSON and legacy reads.
- [ ] For higher-level isolated fixtures, demonstrate authoritative test entitlement explicitly; do not treat imported spell data or closing a class investigation as player eligibility. Publish any missing production-eligibility implementation prerequisite before enabling discovery.

## Hard prerequisites

- #203
- #352

Only these are hard prerequisites: source record/contract owners and the exact shared fixture named above. Class production eligibility stays unavailable where explicitly excluded. Every terminal implementation directly blocks both #279 and #280. A spike must add all of its resulting terminal implementation blockers to both gates before closure; decision closure supplies no playable evidence.

## Verification

`go test -short -race ./...` and `go vet ./...`. Runtime PRs must additionally run isolated PostgreSQL handler tests with `-tags=integration`, injectable dice, rollback, receipt replay and reload (short tests do not include them). Changed UI requires build/lint and desktop/phone confirmation/reconnect journeys. Spike PRs validate source/manifest and read back every published body, parent and dependency, checking acyclicity.

## Boundaries and exclusions

Start in `internal/rules/srd521`, `internal/game`, `internal/engine`, `internal/combat` and relevant handler fixtures. Keep the shared web/TUI action path; no production migration execution or deployment. No general antimagic, curses, nonspell magic-item removal, object/area targeting, higher-level checks/upcasting or automatic class advancement. No Full Rules claim. Retain CC-BY-4.0 attribution and mark adaptations. Close from the merged PR.

Inject history-write failure and prove complete rollback; retry same action ID returns the committed receipt with no extra roll, charge or effect. Reload/reconnect resumes exact identities and pending timing.
- [ ] Disclosure negatives: preview never rolls/writes; reject foreign campaign/actor IDs, hidden recipients and forged costs/timing; public receipts omit private NPC HP, unobserved spells and tactics. Unknown facts fail closed with an explicit reason. Preserve unrelated JSON and legacy reads.

## Hard prerequisites

- #203
- #352

Only these are hard prerequisites: source record/contract owners and the exact shared fixture named above. Class production eligibility stays unavailable where explicitly excluded. Every terminal implementation directly blocks both #279 and #280. A spike must add all of its resulting terminal implementation blockers to both gates before closure; decision closure supplies no playable evidence.

`go test -short -race ./...` and `go vet ./...`. Runtime PRs must additionally run isolated PostgreSQL handler tests with `-tags=integration`, injectable dice, rollback, receipt replay and reload (short tests do not include them). Changed UI requires build/lint and desktop/phone confirmation/reconnect journeys. Spike PRs validate source/manifest and read back every published body, parent and dependency, checking acyclicity.

Start in `internal/rules/srd521`, `internal/game`, `internal/engine`, `internal/combat` and relevant handler fixtures. Wall of Stone
Level 5 Evocation (Druid, Sorcerer, Wizard)
Casting Time: Action
Range: 120 feet
Components: V, S, M (a cube of granite)
Duration: Concentration, up to 10 minutes
A nonmagical wall of solid stone springs into exis-
tence at a point you choose within range. The wall
is 6 inches thick and is composed of ten 10-foot-by-
10-foot panels. Each panel must be contiguous with
another panel. Alternatively, you can create 10-foot-
by-20-foot panels that are only 3 inches thick.
If the wall cuts through a creature’s space when
it appears, the creature is pushed to one side of the
wall (you choose which side). If a creature would
be surrounded on all sides by the wall (or the wall
and another solid surface), that creature can make
a Dexterity saving throw. On a success, it can use its
Reaction to move up to its Speed so that it is no lon-
ger enclosed by the wall.
The wall can have any shape you desire, though it
can’t occupy the same space as a creature or object.
The wall doesn’t need to be vertical or rest on a firm
foundation. It must, however, merge with and be
solidly supported by existing stone. Thus, you can
use this spell to bridge a chasm or create a ramp.
If you create a span greater than 20 feet in length,
you must halve the size of each panel to create sup-
ports. You can crudely shape the wall to create bat-
tlements and the like.
The wall is an object made of stone that can be
damaged and thus breached. Each panel has AC 15
and 30 Hit Points per inch of thickness, and it has
Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage. Reducing
a panel to 0 Hit Points destroys it and might cause
connected panels to collapse at the GM’s discretion.
If you maintain your Concentration on this spell
for its full duration, the wall becomes permanent
and can’t be dispelled. Otherwise, the wall disap-
pears when the spell ends.
